items.say: This is Flask. Twenty-four source files, about seventy-five thousand tokens. Opening a repository like this for the first time, where do you start reading?
items.caption: This is Flask: 24 source files, about 75,000 tokens. Where do you start reading?

items.say: Codebase Explorer cuts every file at its functions, classes and methods: four hundred and forty-seven of them here. Then it traces the calls between them. This step is ordinary code. No model is involved.
items.caption: Codebase Explorer cuts every file at its functions, classes and methods: 447 of them here. Then it traces the calls between them. This step is ordinary code. No model is involved.

items.say: A language model writes what each one does, explaining small related ones together. That gives two hundred and ninety-three units. A program then groups units that call each other, sit close together and are described in similar words.
items.caption: A language model writes what each one does, explaining small related ones together. That gives 293 units. A program then groups units that call each other, sit close together and are described in similar words.

items.say: The same explanations and calls always give the same tree. The model only names the modules. It cannot move anything. The result is a map of the system. For Flask, it has eight parts.
items.caption: The same explanations and calls always give the same tree. The model only names the modules. It cannot move anything. The result is a map of the system. For Flask, it has 8 parts.

items.say: The foundations: the scaffold and blueprint base that the app and blueprints build on.
The running app: the request lifecycle, the contexts that hold per-request state, and the testing tools.
Templates, views and wrappers: the view layer.
Configuration, loaded from files, objects and environment variables.
Jason providers, and a tagged serializer for types Jason does not have.
items.caption: JSON providers, and a tagged serializer for types JSON does not have.

items.say: And the command line, with the public helper functions.
Open one module. Each unit has its signature, a short explanation written for people, and a link to the exact source lines.

Explanations are summaries. Exact facts stay in the code. So you, or your coding agent, can ask. C B E find locates a symbol. C B E source prints it from the frozen snapshot, after checking the file's hash.
items.caption: Explanations are summaries. Exact facts stay in the code. So you, or your coding agent, can ask. cbe find locates a symbol. cbe source prints it from the frozen snapshot, after checking the file's hash.
